propositions: Rebar must support credential injection across eight external providers (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira) and eight deployment/execution environments (local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, AWS-hosted, CLI, library, MCP, hosted-service) without weakening SDK-native refresh, workload identity, or credential-helper protection.

Current _bridge_runner implementation copies the full parent environment to child processes, exposing unrelated credentials (Jira, LLM, cloud) to ticket delivery and reconciler; RP-04 must replace this with adapter-owned baseline plus only the selected auth capability.

Mature OSS prior art (Terraform, GitHub CLI, Airflow, keyring) delegates authentication to official SDK chains, provider runtimes, and helpers rather than implementing a universal secret-broker abstraction; a typed injection model is preferred over a generic string-lookup get_secret() pattern.

The research identified credential shape, refresh ownership, authoritative mechanisms, and failure-redaction obligations for all named providers and environments through primary-source consultation; no universal hot-rotation is feasible without official provider refresh or explicit file re-read in long-lived processes.

MCP schemas and arguments must never accept raw credentials or allow lower-trust callers to select stronger server identity; environment rotation requires process restart unless an official provider implements automatic refresh.

Recommended design includes non-secret immutable config snapshots, official SDK/client/helper authentication by default, typed injection of constructed clients/providers/auth objects, and narrowly typed static credentials materialized only at adapters that require them—no core universal get_secret() or built-in cloud secret-manager.
